extracted.intended_audience: Applicants filing PCT international patent applications; patent attorneys and agents; receiving Offices and International Searching/Preliminary Examining Authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on formal, linguistic, physical and fee requirements and procedural steps for filing and processing an international (PCT) application at the receiving Office, including translation, copy, fee, confidentiality and filing-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of abstract after international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 38.3 — The applicant is entitled, until the expiration of one month from the date of mailing of the international search report, to submit to the International Searching Authority proposed modifications of the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is up to the International Searching Authority to decide whether to modify the abstract accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of immoral/irrelevant matter in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 21(6), Rule 9 — The international application may not contain matter contrary to morality or public order, disparaging statements or obviously irrelevant or unnecessary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the receiving Office, ISA, Authority for supplementary search or IB note lack of compliance with Rule 9, they may suggest the applicant correct the application; procedure to correct defects under Rule 9 referenced (para 6.052).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed technical terminology and signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 10 — There are certain requirements as to the technical terminology and signs to be used (metric system, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such prescribed technical terminology will be accepted by all designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 3(4)(ii), Article 14(1)(a)(v), Rule 11 — The international application must comply with physical requirements concerning fitness for reproduction, paper to be used, manner of writing (generally typewritten or printed), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are in Rule 11 and are generally similar to requirements applied by major national Patent Offices and regional Offices (EPO, Eurasian).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transliteration/translation of non-Latin names and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 4.16 — Where any name or address is written in characters other than those of the Latin alphabet (for example, Chinese, Cyrillic or Japanese), it must be transliterated or translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 4.16 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies to be filed and handling of fewer copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 11.1(a), Rule 11.1(b), Rule 21 — An international application (and, where applicable, its translation) must be filed in one, two or three copies depending on the receiving Office's requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must eventually be three copies (home, record, search). If fewer are filed, the receiving Office prepares additional copies and may charge a fee (Annex C contains Office-specific information).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a translation of the international application is required (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 12.1 — A translation is required when the international application was filed in a language accepted by the receiving Office but not by the International Searching Authority which is to carry out the international search, or when the filing language is not a language of publication and/or not accepted by the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to paragraphs 6.013–6.023 for details; timing and which language to translate into depend on whether the ISA and/or the language of publication accept the filing language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements when ISA does not accept the filing language
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 12.3 — If the filing language is not accepted by the ISA to carry out the international search, the applicant must furnish a translation into a language that is both accepted by that ISA and is a language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless filed in a language of publication, the translation language must also be one in which international applications may be filed with that receiving Office. Sequence listing language-dependent free text may require separate translation (see para 6.014).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements when filing language is accepted by ISA but not a language of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 12.4 — If the filing language is accepted by the RO and ISA but is not a language of publication, the applicant must still furnish a translation of the application into a publication language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case the receiving Office forwards record and home copy (and keeps home copy translation) but does not forward a translation to the ISA; see paragraphs 6.013–6.023 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation handling and copy forwarding upon receipt of translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 12.3, 12.4, Rule 21.1, Rule 22.1(a), Rule 23.1(a), Section 305bis — When the receiving Office receives the translation, it forwards one copy to the IB (record-copy translation), keeps one (home-copy translation) and forwards the third copy together with the request to the ISA (search-copy translation) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the translation is filed by the applicant in fewer than the required number of copies, the receiving Office prepares additional copy(ies) and may charge a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements for International Preliminary Examination Authority (IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 62.1(i), Section 420 — Where the IPEA is not part of the same Office/organization as the ISA, the IB will send copies of the application and ISR and written opinion to the IPEA; if neither filing nor publication language is accepted by the IPEA, the applicant must furnish a translation of the application with the demand into a language accepted by that IPEA and a language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ISA and IPEA are part of the same Office/organization, no such translation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three kinds of fees due for every international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 3(4)(iv), Rule 14, Rule 16.1, Rule 15.1, Rule 96 — There are three kinds of fee: (i) transmittal fee (to the receiving Office), (ii) search fee (to the ISA), and (iii) international filing fee (to the IB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes: transmittal fee for receipt/checking/transmission tasks; search fee for carrying out international search and establishing the ISR and written opinion; international filing fee for IB tasks including publication and certain communications and issuance of certain reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: To whom the fees are payable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 14.1(a), Rule 15.1, Rule 16.1(b) — All three fees are payable to the receiving Office with which the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office transfers the international filing fee to the IB and the search fee to the ISA or onward as prescribed (Annex G of Administrative Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency in which fees are payable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 14.1(b), Rule 15.2, Rule 16.1(b) — Generally fees are payable in the currency of the country in which the receiving Office is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Office-specific information is contained in Annex C and for search fees in Annex D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts of fees and dependence on chosen ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 14.1(b), Rule 15.2, Rule 16.1(a) — Annex C and Annex D indicate the amounts. Where the applicant can choose among ISAs, the search fee amount depends on which ISA is chosen and must be indicated in the request and fee calculation sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Annexes for concrete amounts and Office-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for 90% reduction of international filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule of Fees item 5 — A natural person who is a national of and resides in a State whose per capita GDP is below USD 25,000 (10-year average) and whose nationals/residents file less than 10 international applications per year per million population or less than 50 per year absolute (5‑year average), or any applicant who is a national/resident of a State listed as least developed, is entitled to a 90% reduction of the international filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be true and only owner(s) of the application and not under obligation to assign/license rights to a non-eligible party; if several applicants, each must satisfy criteria. The reduction applies on the basis of name/nationality/residence boxes without need for specific request. The 90% reduction is calculated after any electronic-filing reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reduction for electronic filing and amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 89bis, Rule 89ter, Section 702, Section 707 — Applicants filing electronically with ROs that accept e-filing and in compliance with Part 7/Annex F or basic common standard are entitled to a reduction in the international filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction amounts: 100 CHF where request and text not in character-coded format; 200 CHF where request is in character-coded format and text is not; 300 CHF where both request and text are in character-coded format (or equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific search/preliminary examination fee reductions by certain Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 5.190 — International search fee and preliminary examination fee payable to the Austrian Patent Office, the EPO and the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office are reduced by 75% under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Annexes D and E for the conditions and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: When fees are due / payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 14, Rule 15.3, Rule 16.1(f) — All fees may be paid at the same time; if paid upon filing, no problems arise. All fees can be paid up to one month from the date of receipt of the international application by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates on which payments are deemed to have been received are determined by the receiving Office (same rules as for national applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of fee amount changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 15.3, Rule 16.1(f) — If the amount of the international filing fee or search fee changes, the new amount applies from the date of entry into force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee amount changes between application receipt and payment, the amount payable is that applicable on the date of receipt, allowing applicants to pay within the one-month period on the rates applicable on filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedure for non-payment/partial/late payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 16bis.1, Rule 16bis.2 — If any fees are not paid within the time due, the receiving Office invites the applicant to pay the missing amount together with a late payment fee within one month from the date of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant pays the specified amount (including late payment fee) within that period, the deficiency has no consequences. The late payment fee is 50% of the missing amount or, if that 50% is less than the transmittal fee, an amount equal to the transmittal fee; but it may not exceed 50% of the international filing fee (excluding excess-sheet fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment received before invitation counts as timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 5.194 — Any payment relating to the missing amount is considered to have been received within the due time if the payment is received by the receiving Office before that Office sends the invitation to pay the missing amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves timeliness where applicant pays promptly before Office issues the late-payment invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application considered withdrawn for non-payment in prescribed currency/time
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 14(3), Rule 16bis.1(c), Rule 27.1, Rule 29.1, Section 321 — If transmittal fee, international filing fee and search fee are not paid in prescribed currency and within prescribed time limits (including late-payment-invitation period), the international application is considered withdrawn and the RO informs the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any payment received before the Office makes the declaration that the application is considered withdrawn must be considered as received in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of insufficient payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 5.196 — If the amounts paid do not cover the transmittal fee (if applicable), international filing fee and search fee (if applicable), the moneys paid will be allocated as specified by the applicant or, absent specification, as prescribed by the Administrative Instructions by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office promptly notifies the applicant of the allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of fees (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 15.4, Rule 16.2 — There is no general PCT rule for refunding the transmittal fee. The search fee and international filing fee are refunded where national security prescriptions mean the application is not treated as such, or where the RO refuses to accord an international filing date under Article 11(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RO will also refund international filing or search fee if the application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn before transmittal of the record copy to the IB or the search copy to the ISA, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund conditions for search fee after transmittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 16.3, Rule 41.1 — Most ISAs will refund part or all of the search fee if the international application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn after transmittal of the search copy but before the start of the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the ISA must/may take account of results of an earlier search, refunds are governed by the agreement under Article 16(3)(b). ISAs are free to decide extent and conditions for such reductions (see Annex D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main procedural steps at the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 10, Article 11, Article 12, Rule 22, Rule 23 — The main steps: (i) receipt of application and fees; (ii) formal checking to determine language/form/content compliance (formal nature only); (iii) invitation to furnish corrections where checks show non-compliance; (iv) accord of international filing date where requirements met; (v) transmission of copies and related documents to ISA and IB for further processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks by RO do not go into the substance of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of filing accepted by receiving Office and handling of paper vs electronic filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 29, Rule 89bis.1, Rule 92.4, Section 703 — Each RO specifies acceptable submission means; most accept and encourage electronic filing. An Office that notifies IB that it only accepts electronic filings may treat paper documents as not received, though it may accept them in particular cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RO accepts paper to obtain an international filing date it may require the application be resubmitted electronically within two months of an invitation; failure to resubmit can lead to declaration of withdrawal. Filing by facsimile may be allowed if Office provides facilities and original furnished within 14 days (more detail paras 11.067–11.070). See Annexes B and C for Office-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the international application at the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 30 — The international application is treated as confidential by the receiving Office; third parties are not permitted access to the application before international publication unless requested/authorized by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may publish that they have been designated along with limited bibliographic data; see Articles and paragraphs on confidentiality for further detail (paras 11.072–11.074).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to be entitled to an international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11(1), Rule 20.1, Rule 20.2 — The RO must accord an international filing date if: (i) applicant does not obviously lack the right to file at that RO (residence/nationality considerations); (ii) application is in a prescribed language; (iii) the application contains at least: (a) indication it is intended as international, (b) a request constituting designation of a Contracting State, (c) name of applicant (sufficiently identifying), (d) a part appearing to be a description, (e) a part appearing to be a claim or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name may be misspelled or incomplete so long as identity can be established; see paragraph 6.005 for full conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language-mix rules for accord of filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11(1)(ii), Article 11(1)(iii), Rule 12.1, Rule 20.1(c)/(d) — For accord of filing date, in most ROs the requirement is met if the description and claims are in a language accepted by the RO; other elements not in that language may be corrected later without affecting filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A translation must be furnished where the filing language is not accepted by the ISA and/or not a language of publication. In some Offices Rule 20.1(c) is incompatible with national law, in which case all elements must comply with Rule 12.1 before a filing date is accorded (see Annex C for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: What date is accorded as the international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11(1), Article 11(2)(b), Rule 20.1, Rule 20.2 — The filing date is the date on which the application was received by the RO if requirements were fulfilled then, or the date on which a required correction was received if the filing date is accorded after correction (subject to time limits and conditions for corrections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections must comply with certain conditions and be filed within time limits; see paragraphs 6.025–6.031 regarding sheets received on different days and Rule 20.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment on international filing date and priority rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11(3), Article 11(4), Article 14(3), Rule 27 — Non-payment, incomplete or late payment does not affect the accorded international filing date; however, such defects can lead to the RO declaring the application considered withdrawn later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application that has not been accorded a filing date and one considered withdrawn are both excluded from further international-phase processing, but an application that met filing-date requirements may still be invoked as a priority application under the Paris Convention even if considered withdrawn under the PCT (if Convention conditions are met).

rubrics_metrics.name: RO refusal to treat as international application for national security reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 27(8), Rule 22.1, Section 330 — Each Contracting State may apply measures necessary for national security; each RO has the right not to treat an application as such and not to transmit the record copy to IB or search copy to ISA on national security grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an international filing date has been accorded but national security prevents transmittal, the RO must declare this to the IB before expiration of 13, or at latest 17, months from the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to applicant regarding filing-date accord or non-treatment/withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 20.2, Rule 20.4(i), Rule 20.5(c), Rule 20.5bis(c), Rule 22.1, Rule 29.1(ii) — Where RO accords a filing date, it promptly notifies the applicant of that date and the international application number; where it decides the application is not to be treated as international or is considered withdrawn, it promptly notifies the applicant accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications should be timely and may accompany invitations to correct defects where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation/taking away of an accorded international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 14(4), Rule 29.3, Rule 29.4, Rule 30.1, Rule 82ter.1, Section 312 — If after according a filing date the RO finds it should not have been accorded, the international application is considered withdrawn and the RO declares/ notifies the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB or ISA can call relevant facts to RO's attention within four months following the filing date; such a finding must be preceded by a notification to the applicant and, where applicable, include an invitation to confirm incorporation of missing elements by reference. Applicant has the right to submit arguments within two months or to confirm incorporation by reference. Errors by the RO may be rectified under Rule 82ter.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of sequence listings containing language-dependent free text
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 6.014 — For any sequence listing part of the description, a translation of the language-dependent free text in the sequence listing may be required if not already provided in a language accepted by the ISA as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation must be provided in a new sequence listing containing the language-dependent free text in the accepted language. The applicant may replace the language-dependent free text with the translation or, if permitted by the RO, add the translation so that the new listing contains two languages (one must be English).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for furnishing required translation when filing language not accepted by ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 6.015 — The translation must be furnished to the receiving Office within one month from the date on which the international application was received by that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation not furnished by the time RO notifies applicant of application number and filing date, the RO will invite the applicant to furnish translation either within one month from date of receipt or, if not provided, to furnish it and pay, where applicable, a late furnishing fee, within one month from date of the invitation or two months from date of receipt of application, whichever expires later.
